message.content: For the United States House of Representatives CD-10, Mark DeSaulnier's record on the two central questions is substantial and recent. He sponsored the Block the Bombs Act and the UNRWA Funding Emergency Restoration Act, voted to eliminate $3.3 billion in military aid to Israel through the Massie amendment on July 15, 2026, voted against the State Department appropriations carrying that funding the same day, and voted against the 2027 NDAA linking U.S. and Israeli military on July 22, 2026. In July 2025 he urged Israel to halt operations in Gaza and stated he no longer votes for offensive military aid. He has not called the situation a genocide. Earlier votes, including a yes on a January 2026 appropriations package containing Israeli military funding, sit against this later trajectory. He carries the CAIR Action endorsement and Vote for Peace as a supported ally, alongside JStreetPAC and the Alameda County Jewish Democratic Club, a record that moves firmly against sustained arms transfers while retaining some pro-Israel institutional ties.
